ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.claim: Unlike Genesis' romantic account of Joseph's fortunes, the Qur'anic story illustrates God's unfathomable direction of human affairs: people may hate what is good for them or love what is bad for them.
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.anchor: the Qur'an uses it primarily as an illustration of God's unfathomable direction of men's affairs

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The wife tried to clear herself before her husband and make Joseph appear guilty; the torn shirt served as circumstantial evidence for resolving the dispute.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: if any circumstantial evidence could be helpful in resolving the dispute, it was the torn shirt of Joseph (sws).

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p261/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p261/r8.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p261/r8.claim: The majority read min qablu and min duburu with ḍamma on bāʾ and tanwīn; other authorities report silent bāʾ or three ḍammas.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p261/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: من قبل، ومن دبر، بضم الباء فيهما والتنوين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p261/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p261/r9.speaker: أبو حاتم والزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p261/r9.claim: Abū Ḥātim calls the built form poor Arabic; al-Zamakhsharī explains the terms as the shirt’s front and back.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p261/r9.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم: وهذا رديء في العربية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p262/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p262/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p262/r1.claim: The continuation reports Ibn Abī Isḥāq’s fatḥ reading and treats the terms as feminine proper names for the directions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p262/r1.anchor: دبر بالفتح، كأن جعلهما علمين للجهتين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p262/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p262/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p262/r2.claim: A front tear can fit Joseph following while she pushed him away or his shirt catching as he hurried after her.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p262/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p262/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p262/r3.claim: The truth and lie clauses reinforce what the condition implies; passive qadda hides who tore the shirt.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p262/r3.anchor: جملتان مؤكدتان لأن من قوله: فصدقت، يعلم كذبه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p262/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p262/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p262/r4.claim: Because the witness is from her family, he first makes her truth conditional on a front tear and explicitly names each independent clause’s subject.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p262/r4.anchor: ولما كان الشاهد من أهلها راعى جهة المرأة فبدأ بتعليق صدقها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p262#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p262#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p262#2/r1.claim: The clauses parallel the saying that whoever obeys God and His Messenger is rightly guided, while whoever disobeys goes astray.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p262#2/r1.anchor: من يطع الله ورسوله فقد رشد ومن يعص الله ورسوله فقد غوى

ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r1.claim: A tear from behind means she lied about Joseph and he is truthful in saying that she solicited him.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r1.anchor: أي من خلف يوسف عليه السلام أو خلف القميص ( فكذبت ( في دعواها ( وهو من الصادقين

ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r2.claim: The two conditional statements are either introduced by an implied qāla, as Basran grammarians say, or governed by shahida, as Kufans allow for reported speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r2.anchor: والشرطيتان محكيتان : إما بقول مضمر أي شهد قائلا أو فقال ( إن كان ) إلخ كما هو مذهب البصريين

ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r3.claim: Repeating إن in the second condition signals its independence and adds clarity; the final clauses reinforce what the preceding statements already imply.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r3.anchor: والإظهار في موضع الإضمار في الشرطية الثانية ليدل على الإستقلال مع رعاية زيادة الإيضاح

ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains a front tear as consistent with her pushing Joseph away, or with him hurrying after her and tripping on his garment.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r4.anchor: أنه إذا كان تابعها وهي دافعته عن نفسه قدت قميصه من قدام بالدفع وثانيهما أن يسرع إليها ليلحقها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r5.speaker: ابن المنير
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r5.claim: Ibn al-Munīr argues that either proposed front-tear scenario could also occur when she was pursuing him; pulling is the likelier cause.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r5.anchor: تعقب ابن المنير الوجه الأول بأن ما قرر في إتباعه لها يحتمل مثله في إتباعها له

ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r6.claim: The author answers that the rapid encounter favors the simplest movement: if she chased him, a rear tear is the easier pull and needs no turn back.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r6.anchor: لا تحتمل إلا أيسر ما يمكن وأسرعه وعلى تقدير إتباعها له تعين القد من دبر لأنه أهون الجذبين

ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r7.claim: If she pursued him and he tripped while escaping, it is natural that she would cling to him and tear the back of the shirt.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r7.anchor: إذا تعثر الفار يتعلق به التابع متشبها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r8.speaker: الفاضل المتعقب
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r8.claim: A later critic says that if the witness was an infant, his declaration alone would prove Joseph's innocence; the shirt signs need not match the result.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r8.anchor: وذكر الفاضل المتعقب أن الحق في هذا الفصل أن يقال : إن الشاهد المذكور إن كان صبيا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r9.speaker: الفاضل المتعقب
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r9.claim: If the witness was an observing relative, he used the shirt sign to avoid publicly shaming her while relying on the known rear tear.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r9.anchor: وإن كان قريبا لها بصر بها من حيث لا تشعر فهذا والله تعالى أعلم كان من حقه أن يصرح بما رأى

ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r10.speaker: الفاضل المتعقب
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r10.claim: On that account, the witness mentions the nonexistent front tear first to appear impartial, while passive wording conceals who caused the actual tear.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p221#2/r10.anchor: وبنى ( قد ) لما لم يسم فاعله 4 في الموضعين سترا على قده وقد أمارة صدقها في الذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r1.claim: For the infant-witness account, the rear tear is the decisive sign and the front tear is only a setup, so no matching explanation is needed for both.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r1.anchor: والحاصل أن عمدة هذا الشاهد الأمارة الأخيرة فقط والمناسبة فيها محققة وأما الإمارة الأولى فليست مقصودة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r2.claim: For the wise adult witness, the nearest rationale is that a rear tear shows Joseph moving away and a front tear would show him approaching.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r2.anchor: أن قد القميص من دبر دليل على إدباره عنها وقده من قبل دليل على إقباله عليها بوجهه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r3.claim: The author doubts that shirt direction alone would satisfy a wise judge, since that inference is not certain.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r3.anchor: أن مثل هذا الوجه لا يصلح أن يكون مطمح نظر الحكيم الذي لا يلتفت إلا لليقينيات

ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r4.speaker: ابن الكمال
ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r4.claim: Ibn al-Kamāl says the first condition is a counterfactual foil because the witness knew the rear tear actually occurred; he criticizes al-Bayḍāwī's reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r4.anchor: ذهب العلامة ابن الكمال معرضا بغفلة القاضي البيضاوي حيث قال : إن قوله تعالى : ( إن كان قميصه قد من قبل )

ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r5.claim: The witness can mention the possible front tear as though it were true to emphasize that it did not happen, just as someone can deny conveying a specific message despite speaking to its recipient.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r5.anchor: كما إذا قيل لك : بلغت إلى زيد الكلام الفلاني في هذا اليوم فقلت : إن كنت تكلمت في هذا اليوم مع زيد

ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r6.speaker: صبغة الله الحيدري
ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r6.claim: Ṣibghat Allāh al-Ḥaydarī says each tear direction fits one party's account: front if Joseph approached and she resisted, rear if she chased as he fled.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r6.anchor: أن دلالة كل من الشقين على ما يدل عليه من حيث موافقته لما إدعاه صاحبه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r7.claim: The author finds no evidence that the quarrel was phrased in those terms and says a front tear would have exposed her lie immediately.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r7.anchor: دعوى وقوع المخاصمة بالمقاولة على الطرز الذي ذكره رحمه الله تعالى مما لا شاهد لها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r8.speaker: ابن الفرس
ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r8.claim: Ibn al-Faras cites the verse for judges who may decide from circumstantial signs when formal proof is unavailable, including lost property, theft, deposits, and property boundaries.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p222/r8.anchor: ومن هنا قالوا : إن ذلك من باب إعتبار الأمارة ولذلك إحتج بالآية كما قال ابن الفرس : من يرى الحكم من العلماء بالأمارات والعلامات

ALUSI-FULL:v12p223/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p223/r1.speaker: الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p223/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī says the earlier indications against the woman fell short of certainty, so the shirt was added as corroboration, not the sole basis of judgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p223/r1.anchor: وذكر الإمام أن علامات كذب المرأة كانت غير بالغة مبلغ اليقين فضموا إليها هذه العلامة الأخرى لا لأجل أن يعولوا في الحكم عليها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p223/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p223/r2.speaker: الحسن وأبو عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v12p223/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan and one transmission from Abū ʿAmr read qibal and dubur with a still bāʾ and tanwīn, a Hijazī and Asadī usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p223/r2.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو عمرو في رواية ( من قبل ومن دبر ) بسكون الباء فيهما والتنوين وهي لغة الحجاز وأسد

ALUSI-FULL:v12p223/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p223/r3.speaker: أبو يعمر وابن أبي إسحاق والعطاردي وأبو الزناد
ALUSI-FULL:v12p223/r3.claim: These readers pronounce qibal and dubur with three ḍammas.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p223/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو يعمر وابن أبي إسحاق والعطاردي وأبو الزناد وآخرون ( من قبل ومن دبر ) بثلاث ضمات

ALUSI-FULL:v12p223/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p223/r4.speaker: أبو حاتم
ALUSI-FULL:v12p223/r4.claim: Abū Ḥātim calls the built form on ḍamma poor Arabic because these are declinable nouns, not adverbs.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p223/r4.anchor: وتعقب ذلك أبو حاتم بأن هذا رديء في العربية وإنما يقع بعد البناء في الظروف

ALUSI-FULL:v12p223/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p223/r5.speaker: ابن إسحاق
ALUSI-FULL:v12p223/r5.claim: Ibn Isḥāq reads the two direction terms with fatḥa, apparently treating them as feminine proper names for the directions.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p223/r5.anchor: وعن ابن إسحاق أنه قرأ من قبل ومن دبر بالفتح قيل : كأنه جعلهما علمين للجهتين

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:27/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:27/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:27/r1.claim: A tear from behind shows she pursued Joseph and pulled his garment; the conditional may be quoted speech or testimony treated as speech, and calling it testimony reflects its function.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:27/r1.anchor: لأنه يدل على أنها تبعته فاجتذبت ثوبه فقدته. والشرطية محكية على إرادة القول أو على أن فعل الشهادة من القول

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:27/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:27/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:27/r2.claim: The pairing إن كان can mean if it becomes known that it was so, like a conditional where past kindness is stated after a future condition.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:27/r2.anchor: والجمع بين إن وكان على تأويل أن يعلم أنه كان ونحوه ونظيره قولك: إن أحسنت إلى اليوم

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:27/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:27/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:27/r3.claim: Qiraat read min qablu and min duburu with ḍamma as fixed adverbs, fatḥa as indeclinable names of directions, or with a still middle vowel.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:27/r3.anchor: وقرىء { من قبل } { ومن دبر } بالضم لأنهما قطعا عن الإضافة كقبل وبعد، وبالفتح

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2129#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2129#2/r1.speaker: عامر
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2129#2/r1.claim: ʿAmir says Joseph’s shirt had three signs: its back was torn, it later restored his father’s sight, and its false blood showed the wolf had not eaten him because it would have torn the shirt.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2129#2/r1.anchor: عن عامر قال : كان في قميص يوسف ثلاث آيات : حين قد قميصه من دبر ،

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2129#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2129#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2129#2/r2.claim: A wise family witness proposes the shirt as evidence: a front tear would mean the woman spoke truth and Joseph lied.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2129#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : وشهد شاهد من اهلها : رجل حكيم كان من اهلها ، فقال : القميص يقضي بينكما ، ان كان قميصه قد من قبل

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2129#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2129#2/r3.speaker: محمد بن اسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2129#2/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the witness was a trusted man from Qitfir’s family; he reasoned that a man approaches a woman from the front, not from behind, so the tear proves Joseph’s account.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2129#2/r3.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق : يقال : ان الشاهد مشيوا ، رجل من اهل اطيفير ، كان يستعين برايه ويسمع منه الا انه قال :

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2129#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2129#2/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2129#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says her cousin proposed that a front tear would prove her truth and Joseph’s lie, while a back tear would prove the opposite; the shirt was torn from behind.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2129#2/r4.anchor: عن السدي ، فقال ابن عمها : في القميص تبيان الامر انظروا ان كان قد من قبل فصدقت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r7.claim: Most read “in front” and “behind” with ḍamma and tanwīn; another reading builds them as adverbs, which Abū Ḥātim calls very poor Arabic. Other readers report forms with still bāʾ or unmarked endings.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236/r7.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس: «من قبل» و «من دبر» بضم الباءين وبالتنوين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236#2/r4.claim: Jurists who allow judgment from circumstantial signs rely on this verse’s shirt evidence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p236#2/r4.anchor: ونزع بهذه الآية من يرى الحكم بالأمارة، من العلماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r7.claim: A rear tear supports Joseph: as he fled, she grabbed the back of his shirt to pull him toward her and tore it there.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p383/r7.anchor: وذلك يكون كما وقع لما هرب منها، وتطلبته أمسكت بقميصه من ورائه لترده إليها

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r15.claim: A front tear would show Joseph had approached her; a back tear would show he was fleeing from her.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r15.anchor: إذا طلب المرأة كان مقبلا عليها فيكون شق قميصه من قبله دليلا على طلبه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r16.claim: Joseph's shirt is one of three signs: its back tear proved him truthful, the false blood on it exposed his brothers, and its placement on Jacob's face restored his sight.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p27/r16.anchor: وهذه إحدى الآيات الثلاث في قميصه : إن كان قد من دبر فكان فيه دليل على صدقه

MUQATIL:12:27-31/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:27-31/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:27-31/r1.claim: A tear from behind means Joseph fled from her, so the woman lied and Joseph spoke truthfully.
MUQATIL:12:27-31/r1.anchor: أي وإن كان يوسف هو الهارب منها، فأدركته فقدت قميصه من دبر، فكذبت على يوسف، ويوسف من الصادقين في قوله

MUQATIL:12:27-31/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:27-31/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:27-31/r2.claim: They heard the pair's commotion and the shirt tearing behind the door.
MUQATIL:12:27-31/r2.anchor: وقد سمعا جلبتهما وتمزيق القميص من وراء الباب

NASAFI-FULL:v2p185#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p185#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p185#2/r1.claim: If the shirt was torn behind, she lied and Joseph spoke truth; the implied syntax is that the witness said, if the shirt proves to be torn this way.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p185#2/r1.anchor: والتقدير وشهد شاهد فقال أن كان قميصه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p185#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p185#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p185#2/r2.claim: A front tear would support her because Joseph was hurrying after her, might stumble and tear its front, or she could have torn it while pushing him away.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p185#2/r2.anchor: لأنه يسرع خلفها ليلحقها فيعثر فى مقادم قميصه فيشقه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p185#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p185#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p185#2/r3.claim: Indefinite qablu and duburu mean from a direction called front or back; combining future-oriented in with kāna means if it turns out his shirt was torn from behind.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p185#2/r3.anchor: واما تنكير قبل ودبر فمعناه من جهة يقال لها قبل ومن جهة يقال لها دبر

QURTUBI-FULL:12:26-28/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26-28/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26-28/r1.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read qabl and dubr as terminal adverbs with suppressed possessors; other readers use diptote-like fatḥa or shortened genitive forms.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:26-28/r1.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن يعمر وابن أبي إسحق «من قبل» بضم القاف والباء واللام، وكذا «دبر»

NAHHAS:v2p323/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p323/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p323/r14.claim: Abu Jaafar finds it likeliest that the witness was a wise adult whom the king consulted.
NAHHAS:v2p323/r14.anchor: والأشبه بالمعنى والله أعلم أن يكون رجلا عاقلا حكيما شاوره الملك

NAHHAS:v2p323/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p323/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p323/r15.claim: A child's testimony for Joseph would itself be a clearer miracle than inference from the shirt.
NAHHAS:v2p323/r15.anchor: ولو كان طفلا لكان شهادته ليوسف صلى الله عليه وسلم يغني أن يأتي بدليل من العادة

NAHHAS:v2p323/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p323/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p323/r16.claim: The hadith of four who spoke as infants is compatible: Joseph's witness could be young without being a small child.
NAHHAS:v2p323/r16.anchor: وليس هذا بمخالف للحديث تكلم أربعة وهم صغار منهم صاحب يوسف يكون بمعنى صغير وليس بشيخ

NAHHAS:v2p323/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p323/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v2p323/r17.claim: Abu Jaafar says Ibn Abbas repeatedly transmitted that Joseph's witness was not a child.
NAHHAS:v2p323/r17.anchor: وقد تواترت الرواية عنه أن صاحب يوسف ليس بصبي

NAHHAS:v2p323/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p323/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p323/r18.claim: إن كان قميصه is conditional and jussive, though conditionals normally project past verbs into the future.
NAHHAS:v2p323/r18.anchor: ( إن كان قميصه ) في موضع جزم بالشرط وفيه من النحو ما يشكل

NAHHAS:v2p323/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p323/r19.speaker: المازني
NAHHAS:v2p323/r19.claim: Al-Mazini explains the past-tense form by positing an omitted القول.

NAHHAS:v2p323/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p323/r20.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v2p323/r20.claim: Muhammad ibn Yazid says كان is broad enough to express all actions.
NAHHAS:v2p323/r20.anchor: وقال محمد بن يزيد هذا لقوة كان فإنه يعبر بها عن جميع الأفعال

NAHHAS:v2p323/r21.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p323/r21.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v2p323/r21.claim: Abu Ishaq explains إن كان as إن يعلم: knowing has not yet occurred, and كان can express that meaning.
NAHHAS:v2p323/r21.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق المعنى أن يكن أي إن يعلم فالعلم لم يقع

NAHHAS:v2p323/r22.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p323/r22.speaker: زهير
NAHHAS:v2p323/r22.claim: Abu Ishaq cites a line by Zuhayr as a parallel for expressing this meaning with a past form.

NAHHAS:v2p325/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p325/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p325/r1.claim: Zuhayr's line is cited as a parallel for the past-tense conditional construction.
NAHHAS:v2p325/r1.anchor: ( وكان طوى كشحا على مستكنة … فلا هو أبداها ولم يتقدم )

NAHHAS:v2p325/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p325/r2.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر وابن أبي إسحاق
NAHHAS:v2p325/r2.claim: These readers use ḍamma on qāf, bāʾ, and lām in قد من قبل; they do likewise with دبر.
NAHHAS:v2p325/r2.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن يعمر وابن أبي إسحاق ( إن كان قميصه قد من قبل فصدقت ) بضم القاف والباء واللام

NAHHAS:v2p325/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p325/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v2p325/r3.claim: Abu Ishaq treats من قبل and من دبر as endpoints, and permits fatḥa in both.
NAHHAS:v2p325/r3.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق يجعله غاية أي من قبله ومن دبره

STUDYQURAN:12:26/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:26/r1.speaker: Bg
STUDYQURAN:12:26/r1.claim: Joseph’s defense means that Zulaykhā sought illicit sex and he refused and fled.
STUDYQURAN:12:26/r1.anchor: She wanted to commit indecency with me, but I refused and fled

STUDYQURAN:12:26/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:26/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:12:26/r2.claim: Many traditional sources identify the witness from her family as a wise paternal cousin.
STUDYQURAN:12:26/r2.anchor: one of Zulaykhā’s paternal cousins who was a wise man

STUDYQURAN:12:26/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:26/r3.speaker: Kl
STUDYQURAN:12:26/r3.claim: A shirt torn in front would support Zulaykhā’s claim, since it would suggest she defended herself from Joseph.
STUDYQURAN:12:26/r3.anchor: If the shirt were torn from the front, it would indicate that Zulaykhā was telling the truth

STUDYQURAN:12:26/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:26/r4.speaker: Kl
STUDYQURAN:12:26/r4.claim: A shirt torn behind supports Joseph’s truthfulness because Zulaykhā chased him and grabbed his shirt to stop him fleeing.
STUDYQURAN:12:26/r4.anchor: That the shirt was torn from the back indicates that Joseph was telling the truth

TAB-FULL:v13p101/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p101/r8.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v13p101/r8.claim: Al-Suddi says the husband was seated at the door with the woman's cousin; she accused Joseph, Joseph countered that she had pursued him, and the cousin proposed judging by the shirt, which was torn from behind.
TAB-FULL:v13p101/r8.anchor: عن السدي، " {وألفيا سيدها لدى الباب} [يوسف: 25] قال: جالسا عند الباب، وابن عمها معه. فلما رأته

TAB-FULL:v13p104/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p104/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p104/r1.claim: Joseph answers that he did not solicit her; she solicited him, and he is defending himself against her accusation.
TAB-FULL:v13p104/r1.anchor: امرأة العزيز بما قذفته من إرادته الفاحشة منها مكذبا لها فيما قذفته به، ودفعا لما نسب إليه: ما أنا راودتها عن نفسها، بل هي راودتني عن نفسي.

TAB-FULL:v13p104/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p104/r2.speaker: نوف الشامي
TAB-FULL:v13p104/r2.claim: Nawf al-Shami says Joseph had not meant to mention her conduct until she accused him; then he became angry and answered that she had pursued him.
TAB-FULL:v13p104/r2.anchor: عن نوف الشامي، قال: " ما كان يوسف يريد أن يذكره حتى {قالت ما جزاء من أراد بأهلك سوءا} [يوسف: 25] . الآية، قال: فغضب فقال: هي راودتني عن نفسي "

TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r4.claim: The shirt's direction settles the dispute: a fugitive is struck from behind, while a tear at the front would indicate that Joseph pursued and was lying.
TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r4.anchor: لأن المطلوب إذا كان هاربا فإنما يؤتى من قبل دبره، فكان معلوما أن الشق لو كان من قبل لم يكن هاربا

TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r5.claim: Qatada says the shirt itself adjudicated between the two.
TAB-FULL:v13p111#2/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: " قال: يعني الشاهد من أهلها: القميص يقضي بينهما "

TAB-FULL:v13p112/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p112/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p112/r1.claim: The particle أن is omitted before the witness's if-clause because the testimony is construed as speech, as though someone from her family said it.
TAB-FULL:v13p112/r1.anchor: كما قيل: {يوصيكم الله في أولادكم للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين} [النساء: 11] لأنه ذهب بالوصية إلى القول

TAB-FULL:v13p112/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p112/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p112/r2.claim: Al-Tabari compares the ellipsis with the inheritance statement in 4:11, which is likewise construed as speech.
TAB-FULL:v13p112/r2.anchor: كما قيل: {يوصيكم الله في أولادكم للذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين} [النساء: 11] لأنه ذهب بالوصية إلى القول

SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r1.claim: The common reading inflects من دبر and من قبل with tanwin, meaning ‘from behind’ and ‘from in front,’ whether of the shirt or Joseph.
SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r1.anchor: قرأ العامة جميع ذلك بضمتين والجر والتنوين، بمعنى من خلف ومن قدام

SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r2.speaker: الحسن، أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan and a transmission from Abū ʿAmr quiesce the ʿayn as a lightening, a Hijaz and Asad dialect.
SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r2.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو عمرو في رواية بتسكين العين تخفيفا وهي لغة الحجاز وأسد

SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r3.speaker: ابن يعمر، ابن أبي إسحاق، العطاردي، الجارود
SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r3.claim: Ibn Yaʿmar, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, al-ʿAṭāridī, and al-Jārūd read both words with three ḍammas; some transmissions also quiesce ʿayn and build both on ḍamma.
SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن يعمر وابن أبي إسحاق والعطاردي والجارود بثلاث ضمات

SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r4.claim: The ḍamma-built form analogizes to قبل and بعد when cut off from annexation, making the word itself an endpoint; the underlying forms are inflected nouns, not adverbs.
SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r4.anchor: جعلوهما كقبل وبعد في بنائهما على الضم عند قطعهما عن الإضافة

SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r5.speaker: أبو حاتم
SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r5.claim: Abū Ḥātim calls this construction poor Arabic, since it occurs only with adverbs.
SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r5.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: " وهذا رديء في العربية وإنما يقع هذا البناء في الظروف "

SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the tanwin as indefinite: ‘from a side called front’ or ‘a side called back’; Ibn Abī Isḥāq also reads من قبل ومن دبر with fatḥa as feminine place names, hence diptotes.
SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r6.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " والمعنى: من قبل القميص ومن دبره، وأما التنكير فمعناه من جهة يقال لها قبل

SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r7.speaker: المبرد
SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r7.claim: For كان in the conditional clause, al-Mubarrad holds that it retains its past-time meaning; another view makes it future like other verbs, in a clause serving clarification.
SAMIN-DURR:12:27/r7.anchor: هل تبقى على معناها من المضي وإليه ذهب المبرد، أم تنقلب إلى الاستقبال كسائر الأفعال

SAMIN-DURR:12:27#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:27#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:27#2/r1.claim: فكذبت and فصدقت imply قد, which brings a past verb close to the present state; a frozen verb needs no overt or understood قد.
SAMIN-DURR:12:27#2/r1.anchor: على إضمار " قد " لأنها تقرب الماضي من الحالة

TABRISI:12:25-28/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:25-28/r1.speaker: ابن يعمر وابن أبي إسحاق ونوح القارئ
TABRISI:12:25-28/r1.claim: These readers anomalously pronounce min qabl and min dubur with three dammas and no tanwin.
TABRISI:12:25-28/r1.anchor: قراءة ابن يعمر وابن أبي إسحاق ونوح القارئ من قبل ومن دبر بثلاث ضمات من غير تنوين

TABRISI:12:25-28/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:25-28/r2.speaker: ابن جني
TABRISI:12:25-28/r2.claim: Ibn Jinni treats these as terminal adverbs after deletion of the pronoun, like the verse 'before and after.'
TABRISI:12:25-28/r2.anchor: قال ابن جني ينبغي أن يكونا غايتين كقوله تعالى

TABRISI:12:25-28/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:25-28/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:25-28/r10.claim: Min in 'from behind/from in front' marks the tear's starting point; min in 'among the liars' is partitive.
TABRISI:12:25-28/r10.anchor: ومن في قوله { من الكاذبين } للتبعيض لأنه بعض الكاذبين

TABRISI:12:25-29/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:25-29/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:25-29/r12.claim: A front tear would support her claim and make Joseph the aggressor; a back tear proves the reverse because he fled and she pursued.
TABRISI:12:25-29/r12.anchor: لأنه كان هو القاصد وهي الدافعة

THALABI:v5p215/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p215/r1.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v5p215/r1.claim: Mujāhid identifies the witness as the shirt torn from behind; the witness is a judge who says the shirt will clarify the matter.
THALABI:v5p215/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد: إن الشاهد قميصه المقدود من دبر، ومعنى شهد شاهد حكم حاكم من أهلها

THALABI:v5p215/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p215/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p215/r3.claim: Ibn Abī Isḥāq softens “qubul” and “dubur”; the other readers intensify them, two dialects.
THALABI:v5p215/r3.anchor: وخفف ابن أبي إسحاق القبل والدبر وثقلهما الآخرون وهما لغتان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p84/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p84/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p84/r1.claim: The witness’s test and explanation use the shirt’s front or back tear to distinguish the truthful party from the liar.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p84/r1.anchor: من حكم الشاهد وبيانه عما يوجب الاستدلال به على تمييز الكاذب من الصادق.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:27-30/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:27-30/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:27-30/r1.claim: A tear in the back means the woman lied and Joseph told the truth.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:27-30/r1.anchor: وإن كان قميصه قد من دبر فكذبت وهو من الصادقين

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:26/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:26/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:26/r1.claim: A likely experienced family member arriving with the official proposed the torn-shirt test: a front tear would favor the wife, a back tear Joseph.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:26/r1.anchor: Gömlek önden yırtılmışsa kadın, arkadan yırtılmışsa Yûsuf haklıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:26/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:26/r2.speaker: Mevdûdî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:26/r2.claim: Maududi suggests the family witness may have been a judge, though the source says this is uncertain.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:26/r2.anchor: Mevdûdî bu zatın yargıç olma ihtimalinden söz eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:26/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:26/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:26/r3.claim: Whether or not he was a judge, the witness was just: despite belonging to the wife's family, he did not take sides.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:26/r3.anchor: kadının ailesinden olduğu halde taraf tutmamış, adaletten ayrılmamıştır

ASAD-NOTES:12:24#n25/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:24#n25/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:24#n25/r2.claim: The Qur'anic episodes in 12:26-34 are absent from Genesis, where the husband immediately believes the accusation and imprisons Joseph.
ASAD-NOTES:12:24#n25/r2.anchor: the Qur'anic narrative differs from the story as told in the Bible

BURHAN:v1p415/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p415/r11.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p415/r11.claim: The Aziz's wife followed desire yet failed despite worldly power; Yusuf's obedience saved him from prison and brought authority, showing happiness comes through obedience.
BURHAN:v1p415/r11.anchor: فلم يغن ذلك عنها شيئا وقوتها وعزتها إنما كانا لها من بعلها العزيز

BURHAN:v4p63/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p63/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p63/r1.claim: The author urges attention to these verses' arrangement as part of the Qur'an's inimitability, which must be contemplated.
BURHAN:v4p63/r1.anchor: فالتفت إلى تنزيل الكلام في الآيتين يلح لك ما اشرت إليه في هذا فان التدبر لاعجاز القرآن واجب مفترض

BURHAN:v4p63/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p63/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p63/r3.claim: The shirt test first allows the woman to be truthful and calls him a liar only indirectly; its reverse condition gently leads the opponent to the conclusion.
BURHAN:v4p63/r3.anchor: ومثله ﴿ إن كان قميصه قد من قبل فصدقت وهو من الكاذبين وإن كان قميصه قد من دبر فكذبت وهو من الصادقين ﴾

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p398/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p398/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p398/r2.claim: The Qur’anic form qidada is unique; its root retains the basic sense of tearing, as in Joseph’s shirt torn from front or back.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p398/r2.anchor: وحيدة الصيغة في القرآن، وليس معها فيه من مادتها غير الفعل الماضي في آيات يوسف، وامرأة العزيز،

NASHR:v1p234/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p234/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p234/r1.claim: Stopping at wa-huwa mina al-ṣādiqīn signals that Joseph is truthful in his claim.
NASHR:v1p234/r1.anchor: والابتداء وهو من الصادقين إشعارا بأن يوسف - عليه السلام - من الصادقين في دعواه

NASHR:v1p233/r14.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p233/r14.speaker: بعضهم
NASHR:v1p233/r14.claim: Some authorities prefer stopping after “فكذبت” in the conditional about Joseph’s shirt, then beginning “وهو من الصادقين.”
NASHR:v1p233/r14.anchor: ومن ذلك اختار بعض الوقف على وإن كان قميصه قد من دبر فكذبت
